sections.h2: Getting a fast sale done in Alvin
sections.html:
Three things speed up an Alvin sale: clean tax and title records, candid answers about storms and flooding, and a buyer able to close when you need. The city is in the northeast part of Brazoria County, about twelve miles southeast of Houston, so taxes and deeds run through Brazoria County offices.

Alvin grew from 21,413 residents in 2000 to an estimated 30,115 in 2025. Sellers normally weigh an agent listing, a sale they manage themselves, and a cash offer. Cash is often quickest when the house needs repairs, has had water damage, came from an estate, or has a tenant, since the buyer accepts it as it stands.

  • Agent listing: suits a move-in ready house if you can wait on a buyer with a loan.
  • Self-managed sale: you deal with the buyer, the contract and the title steps.
  • Cash offer: a lone buyer, no lender, and a closing date built around your plans.

Alvin is a mid-sized suburb south of Houston with lower prices than much of the metro. Population is estimated at 30,115 for 2025, up 11.7% from the 2020 base, when the count was 27,098.

About four in ten homes are rented, so an investor can be as likely a buyer as a family.

Alvin has long lived with severe weather. Floods, hurricanes and tornadoes threaten the area each year from July through November. The 1900 Galveston hurricane wrecked most of the city's businesses and homes, tropical storm Claudette dropped forty-three inches of rain near town in twenty-four hours in 1979, and Alicia hit four years later. That record is why buyers ask pointed questions about flooding and insurance.

Expect them to ask about elevation, any water that has entered the house, roof age and wind rating. For new construction the city's adopted codes use a wind load of 140 mph and require engineer-sealed drawings, a survey and a plot plan.

  • Ask the city's engineering and permit staff which flood zone your lot is in, and keep any elevation certificate.
  • Gather records of past repairs, including who did the work and whether a permit was pulled.
  • Know whether the house carries flood insurance and what the premium has been.
  • If you rebuilt after storm damage, keep the final inspection record.

Brazoria County also lets owners in a declared disaster area pay their tax bill in installments, described below. That can matter if the house was hit by a storm that year.

sections.h2: City permits and what they mean at closing
sections.html:
Alvin requires permits and inspections for new construction, remodeling and repairs. Before buying a remodel or repair permit, a homeowner must show proof of a homestead exemption, so a house worked on by a previous owner should have its history on file.

Inspections need 24 hours' notice and are scheduled in the city's online MyGov portal, the same place permits are handled. Driveways and driveway culverts need permits as well. Residential driveways can be 12 to 24 feet wide, and the front ditch may not be enclosed. When the lot fronts a state highway, TxDOT must issue a permit too.

If you replaced a driveway, added a room or finished a garage during your ownership, ask the permit office whether the permit was closed out. An open permit is a common reason a closing slips.

The county tax assessor-collector mails the bills. The Brazoria Central Appraisal District, at 500 N Chenango Street in Angleton, values property and processes exemptions. It keeps weekday hours from eight until four-thirty, and the main number is 979-849-7792.

The county tax office offers several ways to pay:

  • Half pay: half by November 30 and the rest by June 30 of the following year.
  • Age and disability plan: four equal payments due January 31, March 31, May 31 and July 31, open to qualifying homesteads and unmarried surviving spouses.
  • Disaster plan: the same four payments for owners whose property was damaged in a declared disaster area.
  • Deferral: owners 65 or over, or disabled, can postpone payment with an affidavit filed at the appraisal district, and 5 percent interest accrues each year.
  • Partial payments: any amount is accepted, and only the unpaid remainder draws penalty and interest.

A deferral comes due when the owner no longer owns and lives in the home, so a sale triggers it. Tell the title company early about any deferral or installment plan so the payoff comes out right.

The person buying your house applies at the appraisal district and brings a driver's license or state ID showing the property address. If you hold a school tax ceiling, ask the district you are leaving for a certificate that carries the ceiling to a new county.

Filings for an Alvin property go through Brazoria County.

  • Estates: offer a will for probate within four years of the death. If no administration is needed, heirs may use a muniment of title and file the court order and will with the county clerk.
  • Mortgage default: for most home loans the lender must wait until the loan is more than 120 days behind, allow 20 days to cure, then give at least 21 days' notice of sale.
  • Tax sales: a former homestead owner whose home was sold for taxes has two years from the filing of the purchaser's deed to redeem, under a Texas Supreme Court opinion.

Selling before an auction date keeps the choice of buyer in your hands.

sections.h2: Selling an Alvin house with a repair backlog
sections.html:
A house with storm damage, an old roof or unfinished permit work can still sell. The difference lies in who carries the repair cost. In a listing, the buyer's inspector writes up the problems and your price comes under pressure. A cash buyer looks at the house once and makes an offer that already allows for repairs, so nothing needs fixing before closing.

Whichever route you choose, gather the paperwork early: tax statements, any installment or deferral agreement, flood insurance details and permit records. Ask the title company to run the payoff figures, since taxes and liens are paid from your proceeds at closing. That sequence keeps surprises off the closing table.

If a tenant lives there, add the lease to the folder. Buyers want to know the term, the rent and whether the occupant is staying, and a clear answer lets them decide quickly instead of asking for time to investigate.

faqs.q: Is Alvin, Texas in a flood-prone area?
faqs.a: Parts of it are, and storms have hit the city hard before. Floods, hurricanes and tornadoes threaten the area from July through November. Ask the city which flood zone your lot is in.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Alvin property taxes in installments?
faqs.a: In some cases. Brazoria County offers a half-and-half split, a four-payment plan for qualifying age, disability and disabled veteran homesteads, the same plan for owners in a declared disaster area, deferral for older or disabled owners, and partial payments.

faqs.q: Is a permit required for work on my Alvin house?
faqs.a: Yes for new construction, remodeling and repairs, and for driveways and culverts too. You must show proof of a homestead exemption before the city sells you a permit.

faqs.q: Who sets the value of my Alvin home for tax purposes?
faqs.a: The Brazoria Central Appraisal District, on N Chenango Street in Angleton. Owners apply there for homestead and age-based exemptions.
